payload.rationale: I estimate a 25% chance that Freddie Mac’s first published September 24, 2026 PMMS 30-year fixed mortgage average exceeds 7.01%. At the usual two-decimal reporting precision, YES requires 7.02% or higher. No current mortgage-rate observations or economic research are supplied, so this is a broad background-based judgment, not a forecast anchored to the preceding weekly reading. General historical experience supports treating rates above 7% as plausible but relatively elevated; my transfer assumption is that a rate below this threshold is more likely than one above it. Mortgage rates depend substantially on long-term Treasury yields and mortgage spreads, not simply the Federal Reserve’s policy rate. The short time until publication would make the latest PMMS reading highly informative, but that reading is unavailable here. The estimate could be too high if inflation, long-term yields, or mortgage spreads have fallen enough to leave rates comfortably below 7%. It could be too low if persistent inflation, elevated bond yields, or wider mortgage spreads have already pushed the prevailing mortgage rate above the threshold.
limitations: No current PMMS readings, Treasury yields, mortgage spreads, or macroeconomic releases were supplied.
The estimate relies on uncertain transfer of historical background to September 2026, rather than observed conditions near the measurement period.
The contract uses the first published national PMMS average, not an individual lender quote, daily rate index, or subsequent revision.
